Absolutely, I'd be happy to help with that! In psychology, we sometimes refer to these words as "vocal tics." They're repetitive phrases that can become habitual and, when overused, can be perceived as annoying or grating.

For example, think of words like "um," "like," "you know," or "so." These are quite common in everyday speech, but when they're used excessively, they can distract the listener from the actual content of the conversation.

Another interesting example is the use of the word "very." When used multiple times in a row, it can dilute the strength of the word and make the speaker seem unsure or vague. For instance, instead of saying "I am very, very tired," one might say "I am extremely tired" to convey the same idea more effectively.

These vocal tics can be fascinating to study, as they reveal a lot about our speech patterns and can potentially impact how others perceive us. If you're curious about more examples or want to delve deeper into this topic, feel free to ask!
